name: Effective Range / Projected Interpolation Degree
details: Interpolation on an $m$-coordinate Boolean domain has degree at most $m$.
proof: For every projection, its effective range has at most $\mathrm E(\mathcal H)$ coordinates. Every function on a Boolean class over $m$ active coordinates is the restriction of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most $m$. Thus each projected interpolation degree is at most $\mathrm E(\mathcal H)$, and so is their maximum.
witness_verification: For #classes/halfintervals with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n-1$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs. The projected/order-shattering endpoint value uses its established finite-class equality with VC dimension.
